_doc: The one-search series on surf_src_sidistic, the harness's sixth program (2026-11-09). The fifth (~/ar_uni, 2026-11-08..09) found ONE frozen recipe that finishes the map from scratch: PPO with a Monte Carlo tree search beside it, whose lines feed a backward curriculum (unr1b3_mcts5, 'run 5': first finish at 8.23B steps, 9/9 at 118.28 s by 17.44B). The user now asks whether the two threads can become one, the way AlphaZero was trained: one pool of spawns instead of two, a balanced use of policy and random actions in the search, and the policy and the value function updated from the search tree. Four slots, one per step of that question, each one run from scratch judged against run 5's ladder (PROTOCOL.md). It is a designed series, not fork-and-flush: one round, no winner is forked. Earlier programs: surf_src_sidistic (~/ar, 2026-10-20..23), surf_princessburglar_b26 (~/ar_pb), surf_unitfarmer2 (~/ar_uf2), surf_za_loop (~/ar_loop), the unified recipe (~/ar_uni). Read autoresearch/README.md. Every number here is a HARD limit that box.py and the watchdog enforce.
goal: Answer the user's question with runs, not opinions: does one search-driven loop match or beat the PPO + search hybrid? Each slot's recipe is frozen at launch, starts from scratch at the TRUE start, champion-free and generic (PROTOCOL.md: the one-recipe rule), and must clear every wall of the map no later than 2x run 5 (autoresearch/ladder.json: in trainer steps and in total simulator ticks). The record (krs, 115.99 s) is a bar to read results against, never a constant.
_field_doc: The sidistic program's grader field: the goal graph WITHOUT corner cutting at lidar cell 32, the field the recipe shapes on (--race-no-corner-cut 1), copied from ~/RL_Surf/maps (baked 2026-10-23 in that program's round 5). start_d 99,675 u is the kill-aware start geodesic the trainer prints at the true spawn (97,768 u on the plain field).
_score_episodes_doc: score.py counts only the first N episodes of an eval (header episode index < N): its score is a max over episodes, so an eval with more episodes would buy lottery tickets (r6b1 scored 98.418 with 54-episode evals of the incumbent's weights). 0 = all.
_rounds_doc: The user, 2026-11-09: 'So the idea is to have just one thread. ... the way alpha 0 was trained for chess, like we didn't have one PPO and one search. We had just one search. And the model kind of updates of the policy were made based on the trees that we generated.' and 'we have one pool of spawns, not two ... maybe more balanced usage of the policy and the random actions ... update the policy and the value function just based on the search ... Maybe it's a bad idea, I'm not sure. Maybe ... this hybrid is actually better, but I don't know.' Then: 'I topped up vast. You can build and deploy parallel agents to run it, just like before'. ONE round (the user's design change of 2026-11-08: a frozen recipe cannot be steered, so a round must outlast the run; no fork-and-flush). 26 h is what the credit pays for at four fast boxes: run 5 needed 6.3 h on a 5080 to its first finish, and the 2x finish deadline (16.5B steps) is ~12.6 h there.
_max_boxes_doc: 4 slot boxes (box.py allows one per agent), no spare and no operator control box: run 5's own ladder is the control. The droplet's ONE fleet watchdog daemon enforces its own cap from the first program's config; this program registers its boxes in that daemon's registry (RLSURF_FLEET_DIR=~/ar/fleet), or the daemon destroys them as unregistered.
_budget_end_hours_doc: Hours from THIS program's start (state.json started) over which box.py spreads the credit above the reserve: 26 (the whole round) at launch; 24 since 2026-11-09 21:25 UTC (operator): the first boxes cost 0.42 $/h against the 0.34 planned, so at 26 the pace left 0.29 $/h for the fourth box and no offer passed. With four boxes the credit above the reserve lasts to about 19:00 UTC on 2026-11-10, not to the round end. The reserve itself is held by extend's burn x hours check and by the box deadlines, not by this horizon.
_max_dph_doc: $/h for the WHOLE box, its disk_gb of storage included: box.py prices offers with --storage disk_gb, and the fleet watchdog checks the instance's dph_total against its own caps (this table is a subset of them). FAST cards first in this program, because a 26 h round is read in steps: measured on the recipe last round, RTX 5080 368k steps/s, RTX 4080 282k, RTX 3090 215k, RTX 5060 Ti 125-179k (the host CPU is half of it). So tier 0 is the 5080 class, then the 3090s, then two 16 GB fallbacks, then a 4090 or 5090 at its old cap; the 4070 / 3080 / 5060 class of 2026-10-25 is out (10B steps in 20 h would not reach the late walls). Caps sit just above the market of 2026-11-09 (5080 0.28-0.31, 4080S 0.41, 3090 0.29-0.36): a 5080 at 0.59 is double the going rate and is not rented (CLAUDE.md: never rent above the market price).
offer_query: num_gpus=1 cuda_vers>=12.8 reliability>0.98 inet_down>300 rentable=true disk_space>60 cpu_cores_effective>=32 cpu_ghz>=2.5 verified=true gpu_ram>=12
_cpu_exclude_doc: Regexes on the offer's cpu_name. vast's cpu_ghz is the TURBO clock (a Haswell E5-2696 v3 lists 3.8 GHz), so it does not catch old server parts: box 56818837, a 3090 on dual Xeon E5-2699 v3 (72 threads, Haswell 2014), trained the incumbent recipe at 57-59k steps/s with the trainer at 5,400% CPU and the GPU 5% busy, against 166-269k on 32-thread Zen 3 / Zen 4 / Raptor Lake hosts (2026-10-20).
_harness_files_doc: The operator's files: at the start of every round orchestrator.py restores them from the main checkout's HEAD over the winner's head, so a branch cannot carry its own caps, grader or rules forward, and the operator's fixes reach every round. autoresearch/NOTES.md is NOT one of them: it is the lineage's memory and travels with the winner. tools/bad_hosts.json is merged instead (the union of every branch's list).
_lineage_keys_doc: Keys of this file that belong to the lineage, not the operator: when the winner changed one during its round, its value travels into the next round's config.json (r1b1 made its scratch recipe the incumbent_recipe on 2026-10-20). Everything else here is restored from the operator's HEAD.
_offer_query_doc: Scratch training here is CPU-bound: the trainer takes half the container's CPUs for physics. A 16-thread 3090 box ran the incumbent recipe at ~36k steps/s (2026-10-20, smoke_x1) against ~420k on the 5090 PC, so boxes need >= 32 effective threads on a fast CPU. Measured the same night on a 3090 + Ryzen 9 5950X box (32 threads, quota 30.7 CPUs, omp 15): ~194k steps/s, GPU 30% busy. gpu_ram>=12 (GB; 2026-10-25): the cheaper cards' 8 GB variants are out, every good card has 16-24 GB.
_incumbent_recipe_doc: Run 5's exact launch flags (unr1b3_mcts5, commit 9eda7009; ~/ar_uni/runs/unr1b3/unr1b3_mcts5/run.json): the October lineage's 89 flags (r7b2_bel at the 10 ms tick, --maxvel 4000, 300 s episodes, --unstuck-max 0.2) plus the search block: --auto-spine with the MCTS explorer at the random end, 6 min per search, banked adoption, and the backward curriculum on 25% of the training spawns (--demo-share 0.25). box.py launch prepends it; a later VALUE flag overrides an earlier one, but a store_true flag (the --respawn-novel / --respawn-greedy family) cannot be switched off from the tail, so a recipe that removes one launches with --no-recipe and its full explicit list. The last element is ONE string (--auto-spine-mcts-args takes the search's own flags as a single argument).
_agent_prefix_doc: Agents azr1b<k>, branches ar/azr1b<k> ('az' = the AlphaZero-style series): new names, so no other program's run is ever scored as a slot's (sidistic r<n>b<k> and unr*, princessburglar pbr* / pbfr*, unitfarmer2 uf2r*, za_loop zlr*).
_budget_doc: No budget_rate_usd_h: box.py's pacer, (credit - reserve) / hours left until budget_end_hours, +10% slack. $44.36 at the start (2026-11-09, after the user's top-up) = $34.36 above the reserve = ~1.45 $/h over 26 h: four fast boxes at the day's prices (~1.3 $/h). There is no money for a second round.
_harness_files_doc_goal: The finish-trigger fixes ride with the harness (the clip-hull goal, the several-trigger finish); sidistic's finish is one plain trigger box, so they change nothing here. autoresearch/ladder.json (run 5's walls and their 2x deadlines in both units), ladder.py and search_ticks.py (the tick accounting) are the operator's too: every slot is measured with the same ruler.
_time_cap_s_doc: score.py's time term is 10 * (1 - best_finish_s / time_cap_s): 300 s, the sidistic program's (the episode cap is 300 s; the record runs 115.99 s).
